text:
Mara: Quick RFC follow-up thread — we need final decisions on fused-attention variants (fused QKV, bias+rope fusion, and the dropout-free fast path). Main concerns: kernel selection logic, fallback semantics, cache/versioning, and evals for numeric drift.

Raj: Can you summarize the concrete options? I need something I can use to implement the selector after the holiday.

Mara: High level proposals: 1) Strict pinning: model config must declare an attn_impl tag; runtime uses pinned kernel or fails. 2) Graceful fallback: try pinned fused kernel, else route to unfused implementation with metrics logged. 3) Hybrid heuristics: selector picks fused when sequence shape + quantization profile match a safety table.

Kevin: I prefer 3 (hybrid). Implementation idea: maintain a small kernel registry with entries: {signature_hash, seq_range, dtype_mask, impl_name, accuracy_guard}. Selector checks registry first, then falls back.

Anya: Important: dropout-free path yields perf but subtly different sampling behavior (we saw ~0.5% token-prob shift in some prompts with temp>1.0). Need automated eval harness to catch regressions.

Lin: Cache and KV compatibility note: fused QKV changes layout of cached K/V tensors. We must version cache keys or include attn_impl in cache key to avoid corruption. Suggest adding "attn_impl" to the request routing key.

Mara: Agreed. Spec decision: include attn_impl in model serving config and cache key. Runtime must refuse to use cached entries keyed by a different attn_impl.

Raj: How do we declare the model-level opt-in for bias+rope fusion? Some models rely on legacy rope offsets and will break.

Kevin: Make bias+rope fusion opt-in per model: model.meta.attn_flags = ["rope_fused", "bias_folded", ...]. During model load, validate a short numeric smoke test (few batched queries) comparing baseline vs fused precision within threshold. If it fails, mark fusion disabled and log an alert.

Anya: Evals to add to CI:
- token-wise KL and L2 between fused/unfused on 1k random contexts
- top-1/top-5 overlap at 512, 2048 seq lengths
- tail-case stress test: repeated prefix extension to exercise KV cache.

Mara: Also add a runtime metric: attn_impl_fallback{from, to} and attn_impl_selector_reason label (missing_kernel, unsafe_seq_len, quant_mismatch, smoke_test_fail).

Lin: For rollout, propose a canary: route 1% traffic to fused when selector would choose it, compare metrics (p99 latency, token-cost, KL drift). Auto-rollout only when drift < threshold for 24h.

Kevin: Example config snippet for model config we can embed in manifests:

```
model: llama-100b-v1
meta:
  attn_impl: "fused_qkv_dropoutless_v1"
  attn_flags: ["rope_fused", "bias_folded"]
serve:
  fallback_policy: "fallback_to_unfused"
  selector_mode: "hybrid"
  smoke_test_samples: 64
```

Raj: One operational gotcha: quantized int8 kernels sometimes require different bias folding order. Selector must treat dtype_mask distinctly. Kevin — can the registry encode operator preconditions?

Kevin: Yes. Registry entry format: impl_name|supported_dtypes|seq_min|seq_max|requires_bias_fold|accuracy_guard_hash. Selector checks bitmasks fast.

Anya: For dropout-free inference paths we also need to standardize sampling semantics (seed handling, dropout removal) so results are reproducible between fused/unfused. Add a sampling-compat layer: if dropout is disabled, ensure same RNG path and scaling.

Mara: Action items: 
- Kevin: prototype kernel registry + selector (PR target: runtime/selector branch) — ETA end of week.
- Raj: add attn_impl field to model manifest schema + cache key change (PR target: model-mgr).
- Anya: implement CI eval harness with the three tests above (PR target: evals/regr-tests).
- Lin: update rollout playbook with canary gating and metrics (doc PR).

Kevin: sgtm. I'll add logging hooks for attn_impl_{chosen,fallback} and selector_reason.

Raj: I'll add a unit test for cache key mismatch rejection.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/runtime-selector branch -> staging (build 1124).

Mara: :thumbsup: Let's reconvene after the staging run results. If staging is clean, we can start a 1% canary next week.

Kevin: noted. I'll post selector perf numbers once the branch builds.

Anya: I'll seed the eval job with representative prompt set.

Lin: I can handle playbook updates.

Mara: Thanks team — keeping this tight will avoid subtle production drift. End of thread.
